chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, or someone else, said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'They are saying that olives stimulate the winds.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Indeed, olives dispel the winds.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the effect of olives on wind in the body?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the popular contemporary belief that olives 'stimulate' the winds (causing illness) by clarifying they actually 'dispel' them, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Prophet's family as sources of precise, practical knowledge (*ilm*) in medicine and daily life. This distinction underscores the scholarly tradition of verifying medical claims against divine guidance, where olives are viewed not as a cause of humoral imbalance but as a therapeutic agent for expelling wind, a concept deeply rooted in both prophetic tradition and classical Islamic medicine.
